independence: Reviewer opened the official Bundestag submission and DBDD report separately, extracted complete relevant pages from archived originals, and compared the exact 2018 draft. This is not specialist review.

checks: Official submission cover names BT-Drs. 19/819 and two accompanying motions; not the later CanG.

Submission PDF p5 broadens the denominator to all addiction-related inpatient diagnoses. The DBDD report p15 expressly excludes alcohol from the selected drug-treatment share and distinguishes specialised DSHS facilities from hospital and rehabilitation datasets.

DBDD p15 reports 47,777 inpatient substance-related treatments and 11,736 selected drug treatments. Multiplying the latter by 33.5% and dividing by the former yields approximately 8.23%. This derived figure is a within-DSHS scale check, not an observed national all-hospital rate.

The exact 33.5% appears in the report's later inpatient-trends subsection; p15 and table4 p16 round to 33%. The final source locator should include the exact-value subsection as supplementary evidence.
The p6 youth-protection passage expressly criticises adult liberalisation. It is an evaluative policy position, not a literal formal rejection motion. A cautious opposition description is supported.
issues.severity_assessment: Major is defensible because excluding alcohol changes the represented treatment share substantially. It does not establish that the author's policy position is wrong.
issues.direction_assessment: True is defensible for the health-risk rationale supporting opposition; no inference about intent.
required_changes: Verify and add the physical PDF page of the exact33.5% trends paragraph; retain the p15 denominator quotation.

checks: Submission p7 explicitly describes marijuana-caused deaths. The matched 32% and 10%/~20% combination occurs in RMHIDTA2015 printedp14 / physicalPDFp24.
RMHIDTA defines the measure by positive toxicology, including other substances; operators can include pedestrians and bicyclists. That measure cannot itself establish causation.

Official Colorado2016 printedp31 / physicalPDFp33 independently explains that FARS toxicology indicates presence rather than impairment and that changes in missing data complicate historical comparisons.
The official2016 table and RMHIDTA figures use different inclusion criteria. Do not replace32% with a different percentage as if it were a like-for-like numerical correction.
The submission separately cites an accident-risk association from CaPRis. This review does not disprove that distinct evidence.
issues.severity_assessment: Major is defensible for turning a positive-test association into a quantified cause of death.
issues.direction_assessment: True is defensible for the road-safety objection; request linkage remains broader precautionary opposition rather than a formal rejection instruction.
required_changes: Ensure RMHIDTA locator is physicalPDF24/printed14 and Colorado2016 caution locator physicalPDF33/printed31.
